body:
The blue-chip index opened Thursday's session higher, on track for its longest winning streak of the year, but declines in shares of Salesforce, Boeing, UnitedHealth and others dragged it lower. The Dow finished the day 464 points, or 0.9% lower.

The Nasdaq traded near flat for much of the day, finishing 0.1% lower amid declines for Sandisk and Western Digital. Both companies reported results that showed strong growth but failed to live up to lofty expectations. [...] Investors have been bracing for potential volatility in SpaceX shares. A post-IPO lockup on more than 900 million shares held by some employees and early investors is ending, meaning the stock can now be sold. The rocket maker's stock showed resilience though, rising 6.1%. [...] Updated Aug. 6, 2026 at 9:22pm ET

# Stock Market News, August 6, 2026: Dow Falls 460 Points, Breaks Winning Streak

## Oil prices gain amid talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

A sixth consecutive day of gains proved out of reach for the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% from the all-time high it set the day before, as it closed its fourth winning week in the last five. The Dow Jones Industrial Average flirted with its own record, which was set in December, before ending just below the mark with a rise of 34 points, or 0.1%. The Nasdaq composite dipped 0.4%, though it's still near its record set on Wednesday. # Wall Street finishes its latest winning week with a fade

© Reuters

Investing.com -- Wall Street on Wednesday ended largely lower in a choppy session, a day after closing out the second quarter and the first half of the year with stellar gains. Stocks opened trading on a negative note as investors digested a mixed bag of labor market data and the first public comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh since the central bank’s hawkish turn last month. [...] Market participants also kept an eye on uncertain peace talks between Washington and Tehran, with President Donald Trump asserting that the "denuclearization of Iran" was "moving along well."

The benchmark S&P 500 index slipped 0.2% to close at 7,484.47 points, while the tech-heavy NASDAQ Composite shed 0.7% to settle at 26,040.03 points. The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average concluded just under the flatline at 52,306.22 points. [...] The mood improved shortly after the open after the release of U.S. manufacturing data and as Meta extended gains on a report that the Facebook-parent was planning to enter the cloud infrastructure market. Stocks then seesawed through the day in mixed fashion before losing more ground in the final hour of trading.
